stories.headline: Meet Stephen Miller, Trump's new chief of staff: 5 things to know
stories.summary: President Trump announced Friday that longtime White House aide Stephen Miller would be his next chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles — who has served in the role since Trump returned to office. Miller is an immigration hardliner and Trump loyalist who has been with the president since he launched his first campaign.

stories.now: The Guardian: Hardline aide offers ‘unwavering commitment’ to president amid fears White House will double down on far-right immigration agenda Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping… The Guardian: Architect of Trump’s far-right immigration agenda is now most powerful unelected figure in government – it suggests White House is moving to a war footing Donald Trump just gave the middle finger to millions of American…
stories.backstory: Wiles ran Trump's 2024 campaign and was named chief of staff after his election win, the first woman in the role. Miller worked in Trump's first-term White House and returned in 2025 as a senior policy adviser focused on immigration and deportations. Republicans lost the House and likely the Senate in the Nov. 3 midterms, prompting questions about how the White House would respond.
